extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (algebraic geometers, computational algebra researchers and library authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (autgradalg.lib, brillnoether.lib, chern.lib): usage, assumptions, purpose, return values, and examples for each routine. Intended to guide users in calling these procedures correctly and understanding their outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: autGradAlg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autGradAlg(I, TOR); I is an ideal, TOR is an optional list of integers representing the torsion part of the grading group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: minimally presented, degrees of the generators of I are the minimal degrees, basering multigraded pointedly, I w = 0 for all w = deg(var(i)). Purpose/Return: returns a ring and also exports an ideal Jexported and a list stabExported. Example usage and printed outputs are provided (shows resulting ideal, dimension, and stabExported list).

rubrics_metrics.name: autGenWeights
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autGenWeights(Q): Q is an intmat (columns must contain a lattice basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: the cone over Q must be pointed and the columns of Q contain a lattice basis; there must be no 0-columns in Q. In the torsion case, torsion rows must be reduced. Purpose: computes generators for the subgroup aut(Omega S) of GL(n, Z) that fix the set Omega S of degrees of the variables of the basering S. Return: a list of integral matrices A with |det A| = 1 such that A*{columns of Q} = {columns of Q}. Reference: Remark 3.1. Examples (free and torsion examples) are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: stabilizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: stabilizer(RL, A, BB, AMON, n0): RL is an ideal, A a matrix (standing for a subgroup of GL(n)), BB an intmat (standing for an automorphism of the grading group), AMON a list of monomials corresponding to the rows/columns of A, n0 an integer such that the first n0 variables of the basering are the T(i), optional: elementary divisors if there is torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering must be graded (see setBaseMultigrading()), cone over degrees of variables must be pointed; there mustn’t be 0-degrees. The vector w must be an element of the cone over the degrees of the variables. Moreover, B must be such that it permutes the degrees of the variables and the degrees of the generators of RL. Purpose/Return: returns relations such that A*I = I; returns a ring and exports an ideal Jexported and a list stabExported. Examples (including Fano 15 and torsion examples) illustrate set-up, outputs (Jexported polynomials, dim(std(Jexported)), getVariableWeights(), stabExported matrices/lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: autXhat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autXhat(RL, w0, TOR): RL is an ideal, w an intvec, TOR a list of integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume/Purpose: basering is multigraded; elements of TOR stand for torsion rows of getVariableWeights(); w is an ample class or the free part of such a class. Purpose: compute an ideal J such that V(J) in some GL(n) is isomorphic to the H-equivariant automorphisms \widehat X → \widehat X. Return: a ring; examples show calling autXhat(I,w0,TOR), setring RR, and inspecting RES/stabExported/Jexported outputs (matrices and exported relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: autX
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autX(RL, w, TOR); RL: ideal, w: intvec, TOR: optional list of integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute generators for the Hopf algebra O(Aut(X)) of the Mori dream space X given by Cox(X) := basering/RL and the ample class w. Assume: there is no torsion. Return: a ring and also exports an ideal Iexported. Examples: PP2 and example 3.14 from the paper are referenced; typical workflow: setBaseMultigrading(Q), define ideal I, intvec w0, def RR = autX(I,w0), setring RR, examine Iexported and basering/dim(std(Iexported)).

rubrics_metrics.name: RiemannRochBN
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: RiemannRochBN(C,I,J); ideal C, ideal I, ideal J. C is a homogeneous ideal defining a projective curve. If C is a non-planar curve, then C is assumed to be nonsingular (this assumption is not checked). The ideals I and J represent a divisor D on C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: returns a vector space basis of the Riemann–Roch space of D stored in a list RRBasis. RRBasis contains a list IH and a form F; the vector space basis of L(D) consists of all rational functions G/F where G is an element of IH. Example: shows computing Riemann–Roch on a concrete curve with explicit outputs (polynomial basis entries printed).

rubrics_metrics.name: symm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symm(l [,n]); l a list of polynomials, n integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of elementary symmetric functions in the entries of l and returns a list of polynomials. Note: makes sense only for a list of polynomials. Example: symmetric polynomials in x,y,z and computing only first two symmetric polynomials for a(1..10).

rubrics_metrics.name: symNsym
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symNsym(f, c); f polynomial; c list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes a symmetric and a non-symmetric part of f in terms of the elementary symmetric functions from c as well as a non-symmetric remainder; returns a list with 2 polynomial entries. Note: constants are not considered symmetric. Examples show decomposition of polynomials into symmetric part (in c(1..3)) and remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompleteHomog
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CompleteHomog(N, c); N integer, c list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials in terms of the elementary symmetric polynomials (entries of c) up to degree N. Examples provided for variables x(1..3).

rubrics_metrics.name: segre
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: segre(c[, N]); c list of polynomials, N integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of the Segre classes up to degree N in terms of the Chern classes from c. Note: example prints Segre classes up to degree 5 in Chern classes c(1), c(2), c(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: chern (procedure in chern.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chern(s); s list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of the Chern classes up to degree N in terms of the Segre classes from s. Note/Example: this procedure is inverse to segre(...); examples show chern(l) and segre(chern(l),3) returning s(1), s(2), s(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: chNum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chNum(N, c); N integer, c list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern numbers of a vector bundle with Chern classes c on a complex manifold (variety) of dimension N; zeroes corresponding to higher zero Chern classes are ignored. Note: computes basically the partitions of N in summands not greater than the length of c. Examples show outputs such as c(1)^5, c(1)*c(2)^2, c(1)^3*c(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: chNumbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chNumbers(r, c); r integer, c list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern numbers of a vector bundle with Chern classes c on a complex manifold (variety) of dimension r. Note: computes partitions of r; examples compare chNumbers and chNum outputs and handle cases where highest Chern class is zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: sum_of_powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sum_of_powers(k, l); k non-negative integer, l list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the sum of k-th powers of the entries of l and returns a polynomial. Note: returns 0 if k is negative. Example: sum_of_powers(7, (x,y,z)) prints x^7+y^7+z^7.

rubrics_metrics.name: powSumSym
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: powSumSym(l [,N]); l a list of polynomials, N integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the expressions for the sums of powers (up to degree N) in terms of the elementary symmetric polynomials (entries of l). Note: returns the terms of the Chern character multiplied by the corresponding factorials. Examples show the first 3 sums of powers and up to first 5 sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: chAll
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chAll(l [,N]); l a list of polynomials, N integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of terms of positive degree (up to degree N) of the Chern character, where the entries of l are considered as the Chern classes. Note/Examples: prints low-degree terms of the Chern character for c(1..3) and terms up to degree 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: chAllInv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chAllInv(l); l a list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: procedure inverse to chAll(), computes the list of Chern classes from the list of terms of positive degree of the Chern character. Examples show chAllInv and that chAll(chAllInv(l)) recovers the chAll output.

rubrics_metrics.name: chHE
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chHE(c); c list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the highest relevant term of the Chern character. Note: uses elimination and is extremely inefficient; included mainly for comparison with chAll(c). Example: prints the third degree term of the Chern character.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChernRootsSum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ChernRootsSum(a, b); a, b lists of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern roots of the direct (Whitney) sum of a vector bundle with Chern roots a and a vector bundle with Chern roots b; returns a list combining entries of a and b. Example demonstrates combining lists a(1..3) and b(1..2) to give five roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: chSum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chSum(c, C); c, C lists of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern classes of a direct sum of two vector bundles. Example: given c(1..3) and C(1..2), prints resulting Chern classes (list including c(1)+C(1), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ChernRootsDual
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ChernRootsDual(l); l a list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern roots of the dual vector bundle of a vector bundle with Chern roots from l. Example: returns -a(1), -a(2), -a(3) for input a(1..3).

rubrics_metrics.name: chDual
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chDual(c); c list of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of Chern classes of the dual vector bundle. Example: for c(1..3) prints -c(1), c(2), -c(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: ChernRootsProd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ChernRootsProd(a, b); a, b lists of polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the Chern roots of the tensor product of a vector bundle with Chern roots a and a vector bundle with Chern roots b. Example: given a(1..2) and b(1..3), prints sums a(i)+b(j) for each pair, producing multiple roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: chProd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: chProd(r, c, R, C [, N]); r, R polynomials (integers); c, C lists of polynomials, N integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: computes the list of Chern classes of the product (tensor) of two vector bundles in terms of their ranks and Chern classes (up to degree N). Example: computes Chern classes of tensor product of a rank-3 bundle with c(1..3) and rank-2 bundle with C(1..2), showing explicit polynomial formulas for degrees 1..5.
